title: Phone layout scrolls as one page

history.detail:
PASS: Gate-1 audit of 69160e5 (HEAD). Sprint file re-read fresh; unchanged since c63bbe0 (planning) apart from a92f169's lifecycle status line and folder move.

R1 MET:
- .card at 900px or narrower is now height:auto with min-height:100vh.
- .body lost overflow:hidden, and .rightColumn lost overflow-y:auto.
- .dateBand, .flowSlot and .leftColumn lost flex-shrink:0, which was only needed in the fixed-height column.
- .body and .rightColumn keep flex:1, which only stretches a short page to the screen bottom.
- A grep of page-level CSS (globals.css, reading.module.css, chartTabs.module.css, date.module.css) for overflow, height:100, sticky and contain finds no main-axis overflow or fixed height on any page ancestor.

R2 MET:
- .enhanced .keyPanel lost height:300px and overflow-y:auto.
- The whole .stacked rule went: max-height:50vh, overflow-y:auto and overflow-x:hidden.
- The sideways clip for the 390px phone chart moved to .leftColumn as overflow-x:clip, which covers both the tabs and the stacked fallback. clip with the other axis visible creates no scroll container, so the vertical axis is untouched.

R3 MET: the mask-image and -webkit-mask-image rules on .rightColumn were removed at 900px or narrower.

Required greps, with every hit accounted for:
- 100vh: reading.module.css line 22, .page min-height (desktop, pre-existing, allowed); line 534, a comment; line 538, .card min-height:100vh, which R1 allows.
- overflow-y:auto: none in either file.
- max-height: none in either file.
- mask-image: none in either file.
- Other overflow hits: chartTabs.module.css line 98, .tableScroll overflow-x:auto. That is Sprint 37's in-table sideways scroll, horizontal only, and not an ancestor of the footer. Line 221, .visuallyHidden overflow:hidden, a 1px helper.

R4 MET:
- The .readingFooter sticky bottom:0 rule (line 646) is unchanged apart from its comment.
- The .reveal:not([open]) > .revealSummary sticky rule (line 796, second phone media block) is not in the diff at all.
- No ancestor of either now has an overflow value: the card, body and rightColumn chain is clean. .leftColumn's clip is on a sibling branch, not an ancestor.
- The 44px castButton floor is untouched.

R5 MET statically, two notes for LiveQA:
(a) Sideways clipping used to come from .body overflow:hidden, which covered BOTH columns. Now only .leftColumn clips. The right column's event and reading text has no overflow-wrap rule anywhere in the CSS. So an unbreakable long token in a Wikipedia event, which the old clip would have cut off silently, would now widen the page instead. That is hypothetical: I found no such content to demonstrate it, and ordinary prose wraps. LiveQA step 4 covers it.
(b) overflow-x:clip needs iOS Safari 16 or later. On older iOS the rule is ignored, and a viewport narrower than 390px could scroll sideways because of the chart. That is acceptable, but worth noting in LiveQA step 8 if a real phone is used.

R6 MET: every rule change sits inside @media (max-width:900px): reading.module.css lines 519 to 680, and chartTabs.module.css lines 235 to 264. The only hunk outside a media block is chartTabs.module.css lines 229 to 233, the section header comment.

R7 MET: the diff touches only reading.module.css and chartTabs.module.css, with no .tsx or .ts change. The stale comments were updated: the "fixed 300px-high figure", the Sprint 24 flex-shrink note, the fade-mask rationale, and the stacked-cap note.

R8: QA1 ran npm run verify at 69160e5, exit=0, last line "VERIFY PASS (lint, typecheck, test, build) exit=0". I did not see Dev Team 1's handoff, so I could not confirm that it carries the VERIFY line or the 390x844 before and after screenshots R8 requires. The user should confirm both are there before dev-done. This is the third sprint running where QA1 has had no sight of the handoff.

No Human Prerequisites. No known-failing tests.

CONDITIONAL: CONDITIONAL (round 1). One defect against step 3: the folded "Reveal the horoscope" bar never

Tested 2026-11-23, about 16:00 to 16:40 UTC, against https://my-little-racoon.vercel.app.

and commit c97b958. git diff --stat 69160e5 c97b958 touches only docs/sprints/state/sprint-38.json.
CI: runs 45208862945 (69160e5) and 45209862306 (c97b958). Both succeeded.
Tools: headless Chromium (Playwright 1.57) at 390x844 with isMobile and hasTouch. Scrolling used
real touch drags (CDP Input.dispatchTouchEvent). Also 1280x1400 desktop, JS on and off, and
pixelmatch.
CDP synthesizeScrollGesture does nothing in this headless shell (scrollY stayed 0), so I did not use
it. Touch drag, mouse wheel, PageDown and scrollBy all scroll the document normally.

DEFECT (medium, step 3 / R4): the folded reveal bar does not stick.
- The summary computes position sticky with bottom 0. But it is the FIRST child of the closed
  details element (DETAILS.reveal, 83px tall: the 69px summary plus padding), and that box is its
  sticky constraint. So sticky can never move it from its normal position.
- A sweep of the scroll position on /date/2026-12-16 shows the summary always at its in-flow
  position, never shifted.
- From y=480 to y=690 the reading section's top is on screen (sectionTop 826 to 616 in an 844px
  viewport) while the bar is partly or wholly below the viewport.
  - At y=540: section 766-1050, bar 943-1012, entirely off screen.
  - After a real touch scroll to y=680: bar 803-872, cut off at 844.
- /date/1969-07-20 behaves the same, from y=0 to 200 (bar 984-1053 at y=0, with the section top at
  808).
- Screenshots: s38-defect-bar-hidden.png (y=680) and s38-defect-bar-hidden-y540.png.
- Repro: at 390x844, open /date/2026-12-16 and scroll until "The reading" heading enters the screen.
  The Reveal button is below the fold, not pinned.
- Probe in my own browser only: making the form sticky instead does not fix it either. The form is
  also only as tall as the details element. The sticky element needs a containing box that extends
  over the section, for example a direct child of the reading section. That design is Dev Team's.
- Likely cause, as an inference: this structure is independent of the scroller this sprint changed,
  so it probably never stuck since Sprint 33. I could not compare live: the pre-sprint Vercel
  deployment (270cafa) is behind Vercel Authentication. Either way, step 3 requires it.

For contrast, the sticky that works: after revealing, DIV.readingFooter ("Copy link"), the LAST
child of the open details element, pins at 775-844 from y=665 to the end of the page.

No mask is on any ancestor. The pinned Copy link bar sits below the text at 775-844 and doesn't

STEP 4, no horizontal page scroll: PASS for all real content.
- 25 dates (1776-07-04 to 2050-06-15, including blank 2031-05-09, 1900-01-01, 2000-02-29 and

STEP 5, no JavaScript at 390: PASS, on /date/2026-12-16 and /reading/0b01c79f-...
- Headings Chart, Planets, Signs, Aspects and What happened stack in the page scroll.

STEP 6, desktop 1280x1400: PASS.

STEP 7, /reading/0b01c79f-73d5-4fbc-afeb-d65da32ae38d: same as steps 1 to 3.

PASS: Live-loop audit of fix commit 22804b6, answering LiveQA round 1 (CONDITIONAL): the folded "Reveal the horoscope" bar never stuck to the bottom of the screen. Sprint file re-read; unchanged since my gate-1 audit.

Scope: compared with the shipped 69160e5, the code diff is reading.module.css only (the other changed file is the sprint-38 state file, which is bookkeeping). It is one hunk, inside the second @media (max-width:900px) block. Desktop is untouched (R6), and there is no .tsx or .ts change (R7).

The fix:
- position:sticky and bottom:0 move from ".reveal:not([open]) > .revealSummary" to ".reveal:not([open])", the folded details element itself.
- The summary keeps the footer background.
- gap:0 is added while folded.

Why the old rule could not work: a sticky element only moves within its containing block. The summary's containing block is the folded details, which is exactly as tall as the summary, so there was no room to move. LiveQA's observation, the bar sitting at its in-flow position, is exactly that.

Why the new rule can work. I checked the comment's parent claim against the markup, because the details is not a direct child of the form in the source. In SavedHoroscope (HoroscopeReveal.tsx) the details sits inside div.revealPanel. However, .revealPanel is display:contents (reading.module.css line 692), so it creates no box. The details' containing block is therefore the next real box:
- the form (app/date/[date]/page.tsx line 82; app/reading/[id]/page.tsx line 93) on pages that can generate;
- section.readingSection (ReadingView.tsx line 198) on the disabled path.
Both span the reading header, the idle text and the details, so the sticky bar has the whole reading section to travel in. That is the same box the unsaved state's sticky .readingFooter uses.

Side effects checked:
- On the readingSection path, .reveal is flex:1 in a flex column, so it can be taller than the summary. Its bottom edge is still what bottom:0 pins, and the summary sits at its foot (the margin-top:auto rule), so the bar stays at the screen edge.
- When open, the :not([open]) rules drop away, the details is in normal flow again, and its own .readingFooter sticks as before. LiveQA's revealed-state step 3 already passed and is not affected.
- gap:0 while folded only removes the 20px/14px gap before the closed details' content slot, which would otherwise leave an uncovered strip under the bar.
- Paint order: the details comes after the idle text in the DOM, so the bar paints over text scrolling beneath it.

Nothing else in the sticky ancestor chain changed since gate 1: no overflow on the form, readingSection, rightColumn, body or card.

Checks: npm run verify at 22804b6 gave exit=0, last line "VERIFY PASS (lint, typecheck, test, build) exit=0".

This audit is the PASS that /sprint-reship 38 --commit 22804b6 needs. It does not replace LiveQA re-running step 3, which is the only real proof the bar now sticks, on both /date and /reading/[id].

Still open from round 1, outside this fix and not mine to decide:
- Step 8 (a real phone) was not done.
- LiveQA's long-word probe confirmed my gate-1 watch item. An unbroken 78-character word in an event widens the document to 658px. No real content does this (the longest word across 25 dates was 18 characters).
Master Controller should decide whether the probe warrants an overflow-wrap follow-up. This fix neither adds nor removes that risk. | commit=22804b65af40596044c4447ae7dd5ae6d91c3247
